subject: Nightingale AI - Dedicated commit surge matrix, SLO fit & procurement timeline
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Nightingale capacity follow-up + initial surge matrix

Laura — great to meet yesterday. As promised, I pulled together an initial view of how a dedicated commit could map to your expected traffic patterns and SLO targets. Attached is a short workbook with the inputs we used (peak TPS -> tokens/sec -> GPU slab mapping).

Top-line summary:
- Current expected peak generation: ~9k tokens/sec across ingestion and chat generation (95th percentile load window).
- Target P95 latency: <= 180ms for 2k token prompts; SLO target appears achievable with a 1.5x safety buffer.
- Recommended initial commit: capacity equivalent to 6 A100-80GB GPUs (dedicated slab) with autoscale burst to 9 GPUs during 3x weekly peaks. This maps to ~13k tokens/sec baseline headroom.

Questions for you to confirm:
1) Are there quiet hours where sustained background inference drops below 25% of peak?
2) Do you anticipate a material increase in long-context (8k+ tokens) prompts in the Q4 ramp?

Next steps: Ben will share a technical breakdown (tokens/sec per model variant + KV cache hit assumptions). If those numbers look right, I can draft the procurement timeline and a mutual action plan for legal/procurement.

Attachment: nightingale_capacity_workbook_v1.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks,

Laura — quick technical pass (numbers are conservative):

Assumptions used (per your stack and our previous benchmarking):
- Model family: open-llm-v3-medium equivalent (decoder-only).
- Baseline KV cache hit rate scenarios: 60% (low), 85% (optimized).
- Typical prompt length: 2k tokens; long-context scenario: 12k tokens.
- Single A100-80GB slab sustained throughput (in our environment): ~2,000 output tokens/sec for 2k token prompts at p95 latency ~120ms (when KV caches hit >80%). With lower cache hits, sustained output drops ~30-35%.

Estimated mappings (rounded):
- 1 A100 equiv @ 85% cache -> ~2,000 tokens/sec sustained for 2k prompts (P95 ~120ms).
- 1 A100 equiv @ 60% cache -> ~1,350 tokens/sec sustained for 2k prompts (P95 ~150-170ms).
- Long-context (12k tokens) changes: effective tokens/sec for serving long runs is lower due to attention cost; estimate ~450 tokens/sec per A100 at 85% cache and P95 latency ~400-500ms (varies with batching).

Translating to your peak:
- Peak 9k tokens/sec (2k prompts typical):
  - At 85% cache: need ~5 A100 equiv (5 * 2,000 = 10,000 tokens/sec) -> P95 ~120-140ms with 1.5x buffer allowing burst -> commit 5 slabs + burst to 7 for peaks.
  - At 60% cache: need ~7 A100 equiv (7 * 1,350 = 9,450 tokens/sec) -> P95 ~150-180ms; recommend commit 7 slabs + burst to 9.

Headroom recommendation: target a 1.3-1.6x safety buffer depending on how conservative you want to be. Given your Q4 long-context risk, I'd advise planning for the 60% cache case initially and optimizing cache & batching post-launch.

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_surge_matrix.csv (csv)

I can run a short synthetic load test against a snapshot of your model to firm numbers if you can grant a test token.

—Ben
Ben Carter

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Nightingale capacity follow-up + initial surge matrix

Laura — quick follow up on ops and procurement gating items: 

Operational notes:
- Warm KV cache strategy: we recommend seeding common prefixes during ramp to get cache hit >80% for the first 2 weeks. That can move you from the 60% -> 80% band and significantly reduce committed slabs needed.
- Batching policy: adaptive micro-batching for requests under 2s latency target; helps reduce per-token cost and smooth short spikes.

Procurement/workflow:
- Suggested phased commit: 6 slabs committed for baseline (covers 85% cache optimistic mapping if we agree the seeding plan), with an agreed burst cap up to +3 slabs for 90 days post-launch while we calibrate cache hit rates.
- Timeline: sign MSA by 2028-09-15 -> provisioning window 8-10 weeks -> target live: 2028-11-10 to 2028-11-24.

Risk callouts:
1) If long-context traffic increases to >15% before cache optimizations, you'll need to increase committed slabs by ~2-3 to maintain P95 <180ms.
2) Cold-start patterns from infrequent tenants will increase tail latency; consider a small shared warm pool for onboarding sessions.

Attachment: SLO_mapping_p95_notes.txt (txt)

Happy to walk through the workbook with your infra team this week.

Karthik Iyer
Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

Thanks team — the numbers look reasonable and align with our internal modelling. A couple of clarifications before we route to legal: 

- We are inclined to accept the phased commit (6 slabs + burst + calibration window) but need the estimate in monthly token quotas and a cost band for the 60% vs 85% cache cases for finance. Can you provide an expected monthly token range and cost delta for those two scenarios?
- Procurement would like any SLA exceptions (bursting, replacement hardware, scheduled maintenance) noted in the SOW appendix.

If you can send the monthly token projection and a short SOW appendix draft by Friday, we'll try to get the MSA request into our pipeline for the 9/15 target.

Thanks,
